title: Invention of the bow and arrow
summary: At Sibudu Cave in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, small quartz tools from Howiesons Poort layers dated to about 64,700–61,700 years ago bear use-traces and residues showing that many could only have tipped arrows. Since wood, cord and feathers rarely survive, such stone tips are the main evidence for early bows; a recent review notes that only some authors accept bow use in the African Middle Stone Age. Arrows let hunters take prey from a longer distance, and bow hunting appears in Eurasia from about 50,000–45,000 years ago.

uncertainty.note: OSL ages of the Sibudu Howiesons Poort layers with the tools: 61.7 ± 1.5, 63.8 ± 2.5 and 64.7 ± 1.9 ka (Lombard 2011).
